evidence.finding: 200 OK on fresh unauthenticated GET. Verified in a real Chrome page, not just raw HTML: scanning the live DOM for recaptcha/hcaptcha/turnstile/grecaptcha/challenges.cloudflare returned ZERO matches, and there are no iframes. No Cloudflare interstitial, no login wall. Single Next.js form, 13 controls, stable ids (#founderName #email #companyName #website #tagline #industry #stage #mrrRange #teamSize #description #traction #consent). Submits JSON via fetch POST to /api/submit-startup. Success string read directly out of chunk 0apch4zqlywp9.js: "Your startup has been submitted! We'll review it and notify you once your listing is live." Page states "Free listing". CAVEAT 1: the form contains a honeypot input named fax_number - the driver MUST leave it empty. CAVEAT 2: two required controls have no SubmissionPayload equivalent and are therefore absent from the field map - #founderName (text) and #consent (checkbox); the generic driver needs to supply a founder name and tick consent outside the payload map or the client-side validation will block submit. Listing is editorially reviewed before going live, but the submission itself is fully programmatic, which is why this is Tier 2 and not Tier 3.

200 OK on fresh unauthenticated GET. Verified in a real Chrome page: live-DOM scan for recaptcha/hcaptcha/turnstile/grecaptcha/challenges.cloudflare returned ZERO matches. No Cloudflare interstitial, no login wall, no fee mentioned. Real submission form present (class "form loader", action="#", jQuery AJAX) with 6 name-addressable controls: name, collection (select), website, content, submitter_name, submitter_email. The other two forms on the page are a Mailchimp newsletter subscribe and a site search. CAVEAT 1: required control submitter_name has no SubmissionPayload equivalent and is omitted from the field map - the driver must supply it separately. CAVEAT 2: success_signal is UNVERIFIED. I did not submit data, and grepping the site's own JS bundles (9e780.js, 55e9c.js, bfc8d.js) surfaced no success-message string - only jQuery/validator internals. The "Thank you" text_present value is provisional and MUST be confirmed on the first live run. Low-traffic site; value is a free dofollow listing, not volume.

evidence.finding: Tier 3 on two independent grounds. (1) Fresh unauthenticated GET returns HTTP 403, Server: cloudflare, cf-ray present, 5650-byte body titled "Just a moment..." containing challenge-platform, cf_chl and "Enable JavaScript and cookies" - a full Cloudflare JS interstitial. Same 403 interstitial on /, /products/new, /launch and even /robots.txt. (2) The public API v2 is READ-ONLY for listing creation: api.producthunt.com/v2/docs states "By default all apps are read-only", and the live mutation reference at api-v2-docs.producthunt.com/operation/mutation/ documents exactly TWO mutations - userFollow and userFollowUndo. There is no createPost/createProduct write endpoint. This is the calibration case: the most obvious "free directory" is not Tier 1.

Fresh unauthenticated GET returns HTTP 403, Server: cloudflare, 5645-byte body titled "Just a moment..." with challenge-platform and cf_chl markers - Cloudflare JS interstitial. /software/new/ returns the identical 403 interstitial. No submission form is reachable unauthenticated; the /manage/ path additionally implies an account. Not automatable.

200 OK and no CAPTCHA, but not automatable end-to-end. /services/new redirects to /services/submit, which is only a single-field URL gate (input[name=url] + Continue). Following it through with a test URL lands on /verify/<slug>, a page whose only form asks for an email and submits "Send me verification link" - i.e. the flow terminates in an out-of-band email confirmation click before anything is listed. The page also surfaces Register/Account/log-in copy. /login itself returns HTTP 403 behind a Cloudflare "Just a moment..." interstitial. Email-verification gate = Tier 3 by the login-wall rule.

200 OK but the 21899-byte response is an Ember.js SPA boot shell - zero <form>, zero <input>, zero <textarea> in the delivered HTML; the meta config block identifies modulePrefix "indie-hackers". Product creation is behind an authenticated client-side route (/product/new returns the same byte-identical shell). No CAPTCHA observed, but a pre-existing logged-in account is mandatory, which is Tier 3 by definition.

Fresh unauthenticated GET returns HTTP 403, Server: cloudflare, 5604-byte body titled "Just a moment..." with challenge-platform, cf_chl and "Enable JavaScript and cookies" - Cloudflare JS interstitial. evidence.finding: HTTP 200 but the entire 86-byte body is a Turbo redirect directive: Content-Type text/vnd.turbo-stream.html, payload '<turbo-stream action="redirect" target="/sign_in"><template></template></turbo-stream>'. An unauthenticated visitor is bounced straight to /sign_in - a hard login wall. No CAPTCHA seen, but an account is mandatory. robots.txt is effectively empty (comment only), so no ToS-level crawl ban, but the login wall alone forces Tier 3.

Fresh unauthenticated GET returns HTTP 403 with a body titled "Security Check | Wellfound" containing cf_chl markers - a Cloudflare bot-detection challenge. The older /company_signup path 404s and its 404 page already embeds a Cloudflare Turnstile widget and challenge-platform script. Creating a company profile also requires a Wellfound account. Two independent Tier 3 triggers.

200 OK, but the delivered HTML contains BOTH reCAPTCHA (2 references) and hCaptcha (1 reference), and exposes zero <form>/<input> elements pre-auth - signup is a JS-rendered, CAPTCHA-protected account creation flow. Also note scope: about.me is a personal landing-page/profile host, not a SaaS or startup directory, so its marketing value for a product launch is marginal even after the manual click. Retained as Tier 3 because it was an explicit candidate, but it is the weakest entry in this file.

200 OK and the page title is genuinely "Submit your AI tool - TopAI.Tools", but there is NO submission form in the response. 200 OK, title "Join Peerlist". Peerlist has no anonymous product-submission URL at all - projects are posted from a personal profile, so the entry point is account signup. The page carries a Cloudflare challenge-platform script and Log in / login references, and exposes only a 2-input auth form. A pre-existing logged-in account is mandatory. Tier 3.

evidence.finding: Fresh unauthenticated GET returns HTTP 403, Server: cloudflare, 5633-byte body titled "Just a moment..." with challenge-platform and cf_chl - Cloudflare JS interstitial. Even /robots.txt returns the same 403 interstitial, so the whole origin is challenge-gated for non-browser clients. Frequently cited in 2026 listicles as a free submission target; that is no longer true for an automated client.

THE CASE WHERE STATIC FETCH LIED. Raw curl returned 200 with a clean, free, server-rendered form (ids #submitter_name #tool_name #tool_url #description #category #submitter_email, radio pricing_tier, button[type=submit]) and no CAPTCHA string anywhere - it looked like a textbook Tier 2. Loading the same URL in a real Chrome page and re-scanning the live DOM found 'turnstile' and 'challenges.cloudflare', plus an injected hidden control <input name="cf-turnstile-response" id="cf-chl-widget-lc7al_response"> that does not exist in the static HTML. Cloudflare Turnstile is injected client-side at render. CAPTCHA-gated, therefore Tier 3 regardless of how clean the markup looks.

200 OK, title "Add your product to Uneed", but the delivered HTML already contains a Cloudflare Turnstile reference plus a challenge-platform script, and only a 2-input form alongside a login reference. CAPTCHA-gated on a fresh unauthenticated request. Tier 3.

200 OK, title "Introduce your startup to the world - KillerStartups.com", and the page is free to submit to, but the response contains a reCAPTCHA reference and zero <form>/<input> elements in the static HTML - the form is injected client-side together with the challenge. CAPTCHA-gated, Tier 3.

A Free Launch tier at $0 does exist, but its stated terms are "Badge Required - Free launches require displaying our badge on your website", 5 slots/day, 90-day queue; the paid tier is $9. 200 OK, title "List Your Product For Free On SoftwareSuggest", and a real-Chrome live-DOM scan for recaptcha/hcaptcha/turnstile/grecaptcha/challenges.cloudflare returned ZERO matches - genuinely no challenge and genuinely free. Classified Tier 3 anyway for a data reason, not a bot-defence reason: it is a two-step wizard (#vendors_details_first_form -> #next_submit, then #vendors_details_second_form -> #final_submit) whose REQUIRED fields cannot be filled from SubmissionPayload - GetListed[phone] (phone number), GetListed[number_of_employee], GetListed[number_of_customer], GetListed[comp_competitors] and two mandatory consent checkboxes. It is a sales-qualification lead form, not a product listing form. Automating it would half-fail in production, so it goes to the user as a pre-filled manual step.

evidence.finding: 200 OK and a real Free Listing tier at $0/mo (30-90 day queue) alongside a $129 Fast Lane. Verified in a real Chrome page: zero CAPTCHA markers, but also zero <form> elements - the page is a pricing landing page. The free "Submit Now" CTA links off-site to a Typeform (https://loxr142exnq.typeform.com/to/RB6ZnEf2). Typeform is a one-question-at-a-time SPA with generated, unstable selectors that cannot be expressed as a durable field map, and Typeform's terms prohibit automated response submission. Tier 3 on both durability and ToS grounds.
